summary: Lexy Moran and Captain Grey, after a telephone-less delay and a failed attempt to get a carriage, decide to walk three miles through the dark to the doctor's house to check on a woman who is seriously ill. Lexy insists on accompanying him, and the walk is filled with dread, the sound of the sea, and the single light of the house. The excerpt ends as they reach the veranda and Captain Grey rings the bell. The passage is a fiction excerpt from Book 12, part 74.
one_line: Lexy Moran and Captain Grey walk three dark miles to the doctor's house, fearing the worst for a sick woman.
key_facts: Mr. Binz suggests that it might be a waste of time to come all the way out after she is no longer there.
Lexy Moran points out that the doctor's house has no telephone.
Captain Grey proposes going to the doctor's house first to see how she is, and says he will return if there is no change.
Lexy insists on going with Captain Grey and refuses to let him leave her at Mrs. Royce's.
Joe and his taxi have already gone out from the garage, so no taxi is available.
An interested bystander says a "rig" can be obtained from the livery stable with no trouble.
Captain Grey says he cannot wait and will walk, and Lexy replies that it is only three miles.
Lexy had already walked that three miles once earlier that day and had walked farther with Houseman in the afternoon.
The pair turn down the lane, leaving the lights of the highway behind, and walk in thick darkness under the trees.
Lexy describes the sound of the sea as "the loneliest sound in all the world."
Lexy notices a single light shining through the glass of the front door of the house.
Their footsteps sound "as sharp as pistol shots" when they mount the veranda.
Captain Grey rings the bell at the end of the excerpt.
